samples.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers name the specific problem behaviors and give strong, similar fixes. B goes further on defaults: it reuses the previous hive's alert choices and sets the unit from the phone's region. It also separates common from rare settings ('More alerts', Advanced, search) and makes Reset undoable with a snapshot. A is somewhat stronger on what to check after release, with review tagging, analytics, a staged rollout and an alert-mute metric, but B's stronger coverage of the other items gives it the edge. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers deal with every problem behavior and propose much the same fixes: autosave, no confirmation on the unit change, default alerts, a safer Reset, and grouping by task. A wins on defaults because it suggests reusing the last hive's alert choices for the next one. B wins on save feedback, since it shows 'Saved' or an Undo message where A shows nothing on success. B also has the stronger plan for shipping without testing: tag the existing reviews, check analytics, roll out in stages, and watch the alert mute rate.

pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers name the four problem behaviors and propose better defaults with copy-from-hive. B is stronger on the save model: changes apply immediately with Undo toasts, sync status shows inline, and the reset is split by scope with an Undo snapshot where possible. A says reordering is 'almost certainly the main cause' of the reviews, which overclaims, while B keeps its claims hedged and lists specific signals to watch after release. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers name all four problem behaviors and propose good defaults, a better save model, and grouping that keeps every option. A handles recoverability a little better, with Undo toasts, a scoped reset and snapshots. B wins on the shipping question: it suggests tallying the existing reviews and support tickets, adding specific instrumentation and running a quick internal task check. B does overclaim by calling the engineering-order layout 'almost certainly the main cause'.

pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers name the specific problem behaviors and propose autosave, removing the unit confirmation, alert defaults, regrouping and moving the reset. B goes further: it suggests copying settings from an existing hive, adds undo after each change, and declines to invent threshold values, while A opens by overstating how much confidence is possible without testing (though A does suggest tagging reviews to confirm the cause). B is more consistently honest about the uncertainty and gives a clear rollout and monitoring plan. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers find the same four problem behaviors and propose similar fixes: autosave, no confirmation on the unit change, recommended alerts on for new hives, and moving reset into Advanced with narrower reset options. A does better on defaults by offering to copy settings from an existing hive, and it is more careful about what is unknown. B opens by claiming the changes can be made with reasonable confidence without testing, though its suggestion to tag reviews by cause is a useful check.

samples.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers recommend explicit modes with a visible mode indicator, undo for Paint, and a deliberate Record. B fits this operator better: it makes Record a one-shot action that can never be left armed, shows the paint value before the operator touches the grid, and asks for confirmation only when an existing cue would be overwritten. A is strong too, but some of its points, such as accessibility and gloves, are more generic advice. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers recommend explicit modes, call out the hidden timing threshold in the gesture model, and add undo, a visible mode indicator, a lock and a test with the real operator. A also confirms only when Record would overwrite an existing cue and names that cue. B is solid, but its points about accessibility and gloves are less specific to this operator, and keeping Record as a mode leaves exactly the risk A designs out.

pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers recommend explicit modes and back that with show-time risk reasoning. pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers recommend the same thing: explicit modes, with Select as the default, Paint armed on purpose, and Record as a separate action with a specific overwrite confirmation and an always-visible undo. It also adds useful show-time details: the mode label sits where the operator is looking, the indicator doesn't rely on color alone, and the selection count stays visible. B's show-lock and hold-to-paint fallback fit a live show well, but its 'revert on lift' rule would force the operator to re-arm Paint after every stroke. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers recommend the same variant: explicit Select and Paint modes, with Record as a separate deliberate action.
